about.title: Porterville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Porterville recorded 4 traffic deaths alongside 246 injury collisions in the most recent year of public data, numbers that represent real families along corridors like Olive Avenue, Henderson Avenue, Main Street, and Morton Avenue. When a crash takes a loved one, California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to pursue a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain circumstances. This is a civil matter, separate from any criminal charges that may follow a fatal collision, and it exists to help a grieving family recover costs tied to the loss: funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the family depended on, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's care, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect Porterville families with an independent attorney who can walk through these options at no upfront cost, so you can focus on your family while someone else looks at the legal side.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in a wrongful death action, generally to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents eligible in more limited circumstances. An attorney can clarify who in your family qualifies.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Starts at Death
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Because some Porterville roadways involve city or county infrastructure, this distinction can matter.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs and lost financial support, but also compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help explain how these losses are calculated in a claim.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How much time do we have to file after losing someone in a Porterville crash?
items.answer: In most cases, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government-owned vehicle or occurred on a road maintained by a public entity, the deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just months. Given that some of Porterville's busiest corridors intersect with municipal infrastructure, it's worth having this reviewed quickly.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to a criminal case against the other driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, even if criminal charges are filed against the driver responsible. The two proceedings operate independently and have different standards of proof. Families can pursue a civil claim regardless of what happens in any criminal matter.
